title: Manual for reporting on 2025 zoonoses, zoonotic agents and on some other pathogenic microbiological agents
notes: The objective of this manual is to harmonise and streamline reporting by Member States to ensure that the data collected are relevant and comparable for analysis at the European Unon level. This manual covers all the zoonoses and zoonotic agents included under the current data collection system run by the European Food Safety Authority. Detailed instructions are provided for reporting data in tables and information in free-text forms. They cover the description of the sampling and monitoring schemes applied by the Member States, as well as the monitoring results. Special reference is made to data elements which enable trends to be identified and the analysis of sources of zoonotic agents at the EU level.

title: Guidance on Selection and Use of One Health Operational Tools
notes: The primary objectives of this guidance document are: (1) To offer structured and quick guidance on the most commonly-used OH operational tools and to facilitate easy understanding of What, Why, When, Where, Who, How to use them, and key outputs they can deliver ; (2) To support users to judiciously select the appropriate tool(s) depending on the country context, needs, and priorities and optimize their usage by providing easy to understand key gist of these tools. (3) Provide web-links to access each of these tools for detailed information.

title: General Guidelines for Surveillance of Diseases, Pathogens and Toxic Agents in Free-ranging Wildlife
notes: The guidelines provides a framework to support informed decision-making in the face of uncertainty and complexity, presenting approaches to enable users to select pragmatic and relevant risk reduction / intervention strategies according to identified risk, context and need. The guidance portion of this document is split into four main sections: (1) Engagement with stakeholders and system mapping; (2) Risk analysis; (3) Monitoring and evaluation; (4) Tools and guidance.

title: Taking a Multisectoral One Health approach: A tripartite guide to addressing zoonotic diseases in countries
notes: The TZG provides principles, best practices and options to assist countries in achieving sustainable and functional collaboration at the human-animal-environment interface. Examples and lessons learned from countries experiences are also included.

title: Ramsar Wetland Disease Manual: Guidelines for Assessment, Monitoring and Management of Animal Disease in Wetlands
notes: This technical report provides practical guidance on the assessment, monitoring and management of animal diseases in wetlands. Designed primarily for wetland managers and policy makers, the report highlights the importance of incorporating disease prevention and control into wetland management plans. It explains the main principles of disease management in wetlands, outlines practical approaches to risk assessment and response, and provides guidance on a range of animal diseases of concern in wetland ecosystems, particularly those with implications for biodiversity, livestock and human health.

title: Guidelines for Wildlife Disease Outbreak Investigation
notes: These guidelines serve two related purposes. First, they set out key considerations and best practices for investigating suspected disease outbreaks in wildlife populations, in line with the One Health approach and standards set out by the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH). Second, they provide a source document that national, sub-national and local authorities can use to develop their own pro- tocols for wildlife disease outbreak investigations, adapted to their respective mandates, capacities and contexts. The guidelines do not constitute an operational protocol and are not intended to be applied verbatim. Rather, they provide the structure, principles and reference material on which a fit-for-purpose local pro- tocol can be based.

title: Training Manual on Wildlife Diseases and Surveillance
notes: This training manual contains the core curriculum for the part of a workshop intended to inform and assist National Focal Points for Wildlife of the World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE) to gather and report information regarding the occurrence of wild animal pathogens and diseases in each of the OIE Members.

title: Guidelines for African swine fever (ASF) prevention and control in smallholder pig farming in Asia. Farm biosecurity, slaughtering and restocking
notes: This Farm biosecurity, slaughtering and restocking] is the third of the series of the “Guidelines for African swine fever (ASF) prevention and control in smallholder pig farming in Asia” which guides biosecurity, slaughtering and restocking practice in smallholder pig farming system which are designed for use by national and/or central veterinary authorities, farmers and relevant stakeholders, especially focusing on Southeast Asian pig industry.

title: Guidelines for African Swine Fever prevention and control in facilities breeding endangered wild pig species for conservation
notes: The aim of the guidelines is to provide ex situ conservation institutions in Asia holding wild pigs, recommendations to improve their level of protection against potential introductions of ASF virus (ASFV) within their facilities. Several institutions already have protocols in place. The exchange of this information and any experience with the situation is beneficial for all. Hence, this document is a summary and collection of knowledge on ASF management being accumulated by several institutions and experts

title: Managing Avian Flu: A science roadmap and action plan
notes: An integrated science roadmap and action plan (the Roadmap) is being proposed. Key principles underpin the Roadmap recommendations and deliverables. They include evidence informed decisions, open and secure science, equity and trust, harm reduction and respectful community engagement. Given the progression of H5N1 within and across species, it is suggested that priority efforts focus on advancing H5N1 fundamental knowledge, data and medical countermeasures. Similar approaches can be ultimately extended to other avian flu viruses, such as highly pathogenic H7.

title: Framework for early warning of animal health threats
notes: Effective early warning systems (EWS) are a critical component of reducing risk. This framework lays out the technical objectives and the structural and institutional set-up for the operationalization and management of EWS against infectious animal diseases under a systems approach, which considers the overall strengthening of animal health surveillance systems and the capacity to implement risk-based strategies and respond to detected signals.

title: Evidence, policy, impact. WHO guide for evidence-informed decision-making
notes: This guide and associated tool repository provide WHO staff, Member States and partner organizations with vetted methods and tools to better leverage diverse forms of evidence for more effective policy and practice in the clinical, public health and health system fields. Introducing a comprehensive, multidisciplinary framework to plan and implement evidence-to-policy processes, the guide also aims to foster better collaboration and create synergies among actors and workstreams of the evidence ecosystem.

title: HALI Wildlife Health Handbook
notes: The goal of this handbook is to enable protected area rangers, game scouts, and park staff to safely recognize, investigate, report, and respond to disease events that may impact the conservation of wildlife and threaten human health. The content in this handbook is adapted from a 2-day short course for park rangers and game scouts developed by the HALI Project and Ruaha National Park veterinarians and ecologists. Wherever possible we recommend this handbook be used in conjunction with a hands-on practical training course.
